concerns.text: T001 creates the directory tree under `projects/PROJ-001-assessing-statistical-power/` while all subsequent tasks reference paths under `projects/PROJ-234-assessing-statistical-power-in-reproduci/`. This mismatch means the required directories and placeholder files are never produced for the consuming tasks, violating the producer‑before‑consumer rule.

T012 refactors `code/utils/` after many earlier tasks (e.g., T004, T005‑T008) have already been written to import the original helpers. Refactoring should occur before any task that imports those utilities; otherwise the earlier scripts may reference now‑removed symbols, breaking the dependency chain.

T001 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but it produces filesystem artifacts that are required by virtually every later task. Running it in parallel with any consumer could cause race conditions; it must be sequential, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.

T002 is also marked `[P]` yet it creates `requirements.txt` and `config.yaml`, which are read by many downstream scripts (e.g., T010, T009). Parallel execution could lead to consumers reading incomplete files; the `[P]` tag should be removed.

T003 is marked `[P]` but it populates the `contracts/` directory used for contract validation by almost every later task. Parallel execution risks consumers validating against partially written schemas; the `[P]` tag is unsafe.

concerns.text: T004 is marked `[P]` yet it implements reusable utilities that are imported by all subsequent pipeline scripts (T005‑T008). These utilities must be fully written before any consumer runs, so the `[P]` designation is inappropriate.
